do: Confirm Brand Registry enrolment, then use A+ to replace the plain description with brand story, comparison and lifestyle modules.
dont: Do not plan A+ for a reseller listing that does not own the brand, and do not repeat the bullets verbatim inside the modules.
why: A+ requires Brand Registry and its job is persuasion the bullets cannot carry.
source: Amazon Seller Central - A+ content guidelines

do: Meet each module's image dimensions and text limits, and keep text legible on mobile.
dont: Do not stretch images, exceed the character limits, or bake essential text into an image only.
why: Modules that break the spec get rejected, and text inside images is invisible to search and accessibility.
source: Amazon Seller Central - A+ module specifications

do: Use the comparison table to differentiate variants or sibling products on the attributes buyers actually compare.
dont: Do not compare against competitor brands or make claims you cannot substantiate.
why: Comparison tables work as an in-page decision aid; competitor comparisons create policy risk.

do: Publish A+ before scaling ads, then judge the ad impact only after the A+ page is live.
dont: Do not scale spend on a bare listing and blame the ads for a low conversion rate.
why: Conversion rate sets the ACOS a campaign can sustain; A+ lifts conversion on the same traffic.
source: Amazon Ads - conversion and A+ guidance

do: Lead the module stack with the single strongest benefit
dont: Lead with a logo wall or brand history
why: The first module is the only one guaranteed to be seen

do: Compare three or four attributes buyers actually weigh
dont: Compare on price or against competitors
why: Too many rows dilute the decision and price comparison invites churn

do: Keep text in A+ images large enough to read on a phone
dont: Bake body copy into an image
why: Image text is invisible to search and unreadable on mobile

do: Show the people and place behind the product
dont: Use generic stock imagery for the brand story
why: Provenance is what separates a private label from a commodity
source: Amazon Seller Central - brand story module

do: Check the module order on a phone before publishing
dont: Approve from the desktop preview only
why: Most grocery and supplement traffic is mobile

do: Keep written substantiation for every claim in A+
why: A+ is still a claim surface and is enforced like the listing

do: Publish A+ before scaling the ad budget
dont: Scale spend on a listing with no A+
why: Conversion rate sets the ACOS a campaign can sustain
